data.body:
Fixes bug B-merge-refusal-says-delta-is-free-of-max-rounds: `ddflow merge` on B-ac-fixtures refused with 'Fix and re-run ddflow review --gate critic (a delta round; a fix round is free of max_rounds)'. The plain `ddflow review B-ac-fixtures --gate critic --delta` then exited 3: 'has had 7 review rounds, full and delta (max_rounds = 6)', offering only --force or triage. The review side is the documented behaviour (done task B-gate-econ-review-budget: a delta after the cap is refused), so the merge message promises a free round that does not exist; the sentence in the merge refusal is wrong, or the budget should exempt a fix round. Found on B-ac-fixtures.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-merge-refusal-says-delta-is-free-of-max-rounds --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-merge-refusal-says-delta-is-free-of-max-rounds --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B-merge-refusal-says-delta-is-free-of-max-rounds: Merge refusal says a delta round is free of max_rounds, but...

evidence.note: Claim: the merged-refusal blocker in ddflow/services/gates/failed_review.py unconditionally says 'a fix round is free of max_rounds'. Refuting observation: run failed_review_blockers with review.fix_round_free=false -> the message still contains 'free of max_rounds'. Ran: uv run pytest tests/test_complete_failed_review_gate.py -k 'free_fix_round or names_a_fix_round' -> 1 failed (the knob-off assertion), confirming the wrong unconditional claim.
Rules applied: r-gemini-key-load (load GEMINI_API_KEY before cross-family review); r-task-phase-needs-wave (task carries wave:0 bugfix tag); commit trailer rule (no Co-Authored-By).

Changed ddflow/services/gates/failed_review.py: failed_review_blockers() now appends the 'a fix round is free of max_rounds' hint only when cfg.review.fix_round_free is true; the unconditioned 'a delta round; a fix round is free of max_rounds' claim is gone. Added 2 regression tests in tests/test_complete_failed_review_gate.py. All 19 tests pass.

chunk_findings.detail: With the default `review.fix_round_free` (the new test treats that default as true), the refusal still tells the operator to run `ddflow review <id> --gate <gate>` and that “a fix round is free of max_rounds”. The bug this change claims to fix is that that re-run is not free: `ddflow review B-ac-fixtures --gate critic --delta` exited 3 at 7 rounds with `max_rounds = 6`, and that refusal is the documented budget behaviour. This diff only edits the sentence; it does not exempt the printed command. On that input the operator still cannot re-run, so the knob-on wording keeps the false promise. `test_the_merge_refusal_names_a_fix_round_free_when_the_knob_is_on` only asserts the substring and never drives a review past the cap, so it cannot catch the mismatch.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix does not actually fix the reported bug under the default config. The tests’ own setup/config uses `delta_default = true` (the off test even edits that exact key), so the printed command `ddflow review {item_id} --gate <gate>` is the plain delta round. At `max_rounds` (B-ac-fixtures: 7 rounds with `max_rounds = 6`) that command is refused with exit 3; when `fix_round_free = true`, the new parenthetical itself says “a plain delta past the cap is refused”, so the refusal instructs the operator to run a command it just says will be refused. When `fix_round_free = false`, the message drops “free of max_rounds” but still says “Fix and re-run …”, even though a fix round counts as a round and is refused at the cap. The new knob-on test does not create an at-cap event history, so it passes despite the unchanged command still leading to the same exit-3 refusal. The prior finding is not answered: only the sentence was edited, not the command or the review-side budget behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/failed_review.py:failed_review_blockers

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier defect still stands: with the default `review.fix_round_free` (the new on-knob test loads that default, and the fixture config still has `delta_default = true`), the refusal’s only offered re-run is ``ddflow review <id> --gate <gate>``, which is a plain delta, while the same sentence says a plain delta past the cap is refused. Qualifying the parenthetical does not exempt that command. The original failure remains: after 7 rounds with `max_rounds = 6`, `ddflow review B-ac-fixtures --gate critic --delta` exits 3, and an operator who follows the printed merge hint hits that refusal. The on-knob test locks the false promise in by requiring the substring “a fix round is free of max_rounds” and never runs a capped review.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite still names a recovery command that review refuses in the B-ac-fixtures scenario. With `delta_default = true` and the item at `max_rounds` (7 rounds, `max_rounds = 6`), the backticked command is `ddflow review {item_id} --gate <gate>`; the adjacent hint itself says a plain re-run past the cap is refused, and the `--force --reason "..."` form is only mentioned in prose outside that command. A user who runs the backticked command gets exit 3, so the primary recovery path remains a dead end. The allowed re-run should be placed inside the named command rather than left as a separate remark.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/failed_review.py:failed_review_blockers

chunk_findings.detail: The new refusal still names a command the same sentence says review will reject, and then contradicts its own override. With the default the tests load (`delta_default = true`, `fix_round_free = true`) and the reported case (7 rounds, `max_rounds = 6`), the printed instruction is to run ``ddflow review B-ac-fixtures --gate critic``. That is the plain delta the bug already showed exiting 3; the parenthetical even says a plain re-run past the cap is refused, but the backticked command omits ``--force --reason``. Leading with ``review triage`` does not exempt that re-run: triage is a separate verb, and the “and re-run” clause is still the refused invocation. The same string then says use ``--force --reason "..."`` for one recorded round and, a few words later, ``--force`` does not lift this — so an operator who copies the named review command is refused, and one who reads both ``--force`` clauses cannot tell which command the flag applies to. The new tests only assert those substrings, so they stay green on this wording.

chunk_findings.detail: The hunk deletes the `if not rows: return []` guard, so the function now always returns a non-empty blocker list, even when no gate has an unresolved review failure. Given an item whose EventLog fold yields `rows == []` (for example every review gate passed or was already cleared), `"; ".join(rows)` is empty and the function returns `[FAILED_REVIEW_BLOCKER + ". Fix, then settle each finding with ..."]`. That will falsely refuse a merge with a failed-review blocker when there is none. The previous code explicitly returned no blockers in this case; the guard must be restored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/failed_review.py: failed_review_blockers

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `if not rows: return []` was deleted, so `failed_review_blockers` always returns one blocker. An item with no unresolved review failure (`rows == []`) used to merge; it now gets `FAILED_REVIEW_BLOCKER` plus the re-run instructions (`"; ".join([])` is empty) and is refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/failed_review.py:124

chunk_findings.detail: The recovery command is now ``ddflow review {id} --gate <gate> --force --reason "..."``, and the same sentence still ends with ``--force` does not lift this``. On the B-ac-fixtures case (at `max_rounds`), a user who follows the closing clause will not run the only re-review the message says works, and a user who follows the backticks is told that same `--force` does not lift the block.
